A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including v3's added appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training, benchmark evaluations, memory ablations, and retrieval comparisons in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds clustering experiments, measured inference latency, combined RAG-memory evaluation, and retrieval-failure tests.

M1.justification: The core architecture, training objective, hierarchical retrieval, and memory types remain unchanged. A limited inference extension is now instantiated: Section 4 evaluates RAG-Wiki combined with parametric memories for the 410M model, whereas v1 only suggested this combination.

E1.justification: DCLM, Wikipedia, the 13 benchmarks, and atomic-number prediction remain. Appendix J adds local retrieval-error scenarios on ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge, extending beyond v1's atomic-number memory-blocking experiment, and includes a scientific-name completion example.

E2.justification: The original baseline, generic-memory, memory-type, and standalone RAG comparisons are retained. Section 4 additionally compares the evaluated RAG-Wiki-plus-memory combination against RAG-Wiki and memory alone; this configuration had no reported comparison in v1.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark samples, shot settings, and training budgets remain. Added experiments introduce controlled embedding/tree configurations, H100 timing for 20- and 40-token generations with HBM or DRAM storage, and accuracy averaged over 16 sibling-memory choices. Appendix A.6 also removes the separately described Qwen co-training configuration; unchanged open-weight results do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends diagnostic evidence: Table 2 tests sensitivity to embedding models and clustering geometry; Table 3 measures routing, fetching, and generation costs beyond v1's hypothetical loading example; Appendix J adds qualitative memory-corruption cases and systematic ARC misrouting tests. Existing design ablations and memory-blocking analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same standard-error bars for knowledge-specificity estimates from 100 sampled examples per dataset. v3 adds no seed counts, repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging routing choices in Appendix J defines the new evaluation measure rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original summary results remain unchanged, but v3 adds clustering outcomes, measured latency, per-dataset scores, and retrieval-failure results. The new combined RAG-Wiki-memory experiment reports 45.7% Avg-SK versus 44.5% for memory alone and 41.6% for RAG-Wiki. Table 13 reports corrupted-retrieval accuracies of 55.8% and 28.2% against its ARC baselines of 55.5% and 27.1%. These are additional experimental results, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The objective, retrieval definition, parameter-count formulas, and mathematical assumptions are retained. Appendix I.1 adds numerical substitutions illustrating the existing memory-size formulas, without a new definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The principal architecture and parameter-efficiency claims remain. The introduction newly claims the first systematic examination of the memory-design choices and explicitly focuses the contribution on long-tail knowledge, leaving improved anchor reasoning to future work and qualifying privacy/editing as peripheral.

C2.justification: Appendix J introduces the interpretation that local retrieval errors produce graceful degradation and suggests hierarchical parameter sharing could provide further robustness. Sections 1 and 6 more explicitly delimit reasoning and privacy claims and identify dynamic or learned retrievers as future work.

D1.justification: v3 adds a paper-specific code-access link, newly identifies H100 GPUs as the experimental hardware, and provides a worked calculation of exact fetched-memory and bank sizes in Appendix I.1. Appendix A.6 removes Qwen co-training batch-size and warmup details. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: The bibliography and dedicated related-work discussion are unchanged. Research positioning receives limited revisions through the new first-systematic-study claim and a more explicit introduction-level contrast with token-by-token MoE parameter access.

P1.justification: The introduction, RAG discussion, and limitations receive localized rewrites and clarifications. New subsections B.1 and I.1 and Appendix J extend the document, while its principal section organization and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 2, 3, 11, and 13 and boxed generation examples, with corresponding reflow of existing material. Figure 3c relocates its legend, and Figure 4b corrects upper-axis label alignment. Existing figures and tables otherwise retain their displays and plotted results.

improvement.justification: Measured H100 timings, clustering and retrieval-failure checks, per-dataset reporting, and code-access information strengthen empirical support and reproducibility beyond v1. The gains are targeted: timing covers one GPU platform and systematic corruption covers local sibling routing. Reporting also remains inconsistent: Table 11's B2-Fetched specific-knowledge scores average approximately 46.7%, while the retained Table 1 reports 45.9%. Overall, the additions improve the paper without resolving all validation and reporting limitations.
